title: How much of the park needs tiles?
description: A tiny park in Dhauli has two square green plots and a walking path w feet wide. The whole park is found by multiplying length by width, the two green plots are taken away, and the answer is checked with g as three and w as one.
teaching_notes: One idea: the tiled area is the whole park take away the green plots. Watch for students who take away only one plot of area g squared.

source: Figure it Out (identities and patterns, question 10)
video_script.why: The child has found a ring of tiles as a big square take away a small one, and now finds a tiled path as the whole park take away the green plots.
video_script.substitution: Write the length and width of the whole park, multiply them, take away the two green plots, and check with g as three and w as one.
video_script.anchor: the plan of a tiny park in Dhauli, with two square green plots of area g squared and a walking path of width w
video_script.payoff_line: The area to be tiled is eight w squared plus eight g w square feet

final_answer.spoken: eight w squared plus eight g w square feet, that is eight w times w plus g

maths_rules: length of the park: w + g + 2w + g + w = 2g + 4w
width of the park: w + g + w = g + 2w
two plots, each g², take away 2g²: 2g² + 8gw + 8w² − 2g² = 8gw + 8w²
video_script.design: One idea: tiled area is the whole park take away the green plots. The plan stays all video in the anchor band; the working board holds each line.
open_questions: The worklist takes the path between the two plots as 2w wide, so the park is 2g + 4w long. If the plan shows a path of width w everywhere, the length is 2g + 3w and the tiled area is 6w² + 7gw. The figure was not visible, so the worklist lengths are followed.

narration: <bookmark mark='length'/>First, find the sides of the whole park. The length is w, g, two w, g and w added, which is two g plus four w.
<bookmark mark='width'/>The width is w plus g plus w, which is g plus two w.
<bookmark mark='mul'/>Second, multiply the length by the width. That is two g plus four w, times g plus two w.
<bookmark mark='first'/>Two g times g is two g squared. Two g times two w is four g w.
<bookmark mark='second'/>Four w times g is four g w. Four w times two w is eight w squared.
<bookmark mark='join'/>The whole park is two g squared plus eight g w plus eight w squared.

beats.on_screen: take away the two green plots: 2g² + 8gw + 8w² − 2g² = 8gw + 8w²

narration: <bookmark mark='plots'/>Third, take away the two green plots. Each is g squared, so two g squared come away.
<bookmark mark='left'/>What is left is eight g w plus eight w squared.
